rows.title: Stop the JVM aborting the openmrs-api test fork on Java 8 and 11
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

Since 24 July the `openmrs-api` surefire fork has been aborting part way through the suite on 2.8.x, which fails nearly every pull request against the branch (#6394, #6262, #6230, #6219, and the last two pushes to 2.8.x itself). Every test that ran passed, so the build reported `Process Exit Code: 134` with no test failures to point at, and contributors have been pushing empty "re-run CI" commits to get around it.

#6399 makes CI keep the JVM's own crash log, and with that the Java 11 failure is no longer a mystery:

```
#  Internal Error (moduleEntry.cpp:263), pid=2394, tid=2395
#  guarantee(java_lang_Module::is_instance(module)) failed: The unnamed module for ClassLoader
#  jdk.internal.reflect.DelegatingClassLoader, is null or not an instance of java.lang.Module.
#  The class loader has not been initialized correctly.
# JRE version: OpenJDK Runtime Environment Temurin-11.0.31+11
```

reached like this:

```
V  [libjvm.so+0xc1828a]  ModuleEntry::create_unnamed_module(ClassLoaderData*)+0xca
V  [libjvm.so+0x61eb86]  ClassLoaderDataGraph::add(Handle, bool)+0x216
V  [libjvm.so+0xf139db]  Unsafe_DefineClass0+0x37b
J  jdk.internal.reflect.MethodAccessorGenerator.generate(...)
J  jdk.internal.reflect.NativeConstructorAccessorImpl.newInstance(...)
J  org.mockito.internal.util.reflection.ReflectionMemberAccessor$$Lambda$1524.newInstance()
j  org.mockito.internal.creation.bytebuddy.InlineDelegateByteBuddyMockMaker.lambda$newInstance$4(...)
```

The crash needs the JDK to **inflate a reflective accessor**. Once a reflective member has been invoked more than `sun.reflect.inflationThreshold` times (15 by default), the JDK stops using the native accessor, generates a bytecode accessor, and defines it into a `jdk.internal.reflect.DelegatingClassLoader` — and creating that loader's unnamed module is what trips the guarantee. Mockito's inline mock maker reaches that path while instantiating a mock, so a suite creating thousands of mocks in one fork gets there reliably.

Raising the threshold out of reach keeps reflection on the native accessor for the whole run, so no accessor is ever generated and the crashing path is never entered.

I checked that rather than assuming it. On Temurin 11 with `-verbose:class`, reflectively invoking a constructor 200 times:

rows.title: TRUNK-6829: Fix case, duplicates, backslashes and escaping in properties written by startup-init.sh
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

Four fixes to how `startup-init.sh` writes runtime and server properties, one commit per ticket. They change the same few lines, so they are reviewed and backported together.

- **TRUNK-6829:** `OMRS_EXTRA_*` names containing any lower case letter keep their case (e.g. `OMRS_EXTRA_mail_smtp_socketFactory_class` → `mail.smtp.socketFactory.class`). All upper case names are lowercased as before. Also replaces the unquoted `tr [:upper:] [:lower:]`, whose arguments were subject to pathname expansion: with a one-character file such as `u` or `e` in the working directory, no extra properties were written.
- **TRUNK-6830:** when several `OMRS_EXTRA_*` variables give the same property, the first in sorted order is used and the others are logged and ignored. Previously the last won on first install and the first on later starts.
- **TRUNK-6831:** extra properties are written with `printf` instead of `echo -e`, so backslash sequences in values are no longer interpreted (differently on each path).
- **TRUNK-6835:** values written to the server and runtime properties files are escaped for the Java properties format (`\`, line breaks, leading whitespace). A backslash in `OMRS_DB_PASSWORD`, for example, now reaches OpenMRS unchanged.

**Behaviour changes:**
- A mixed-case name that relied on being lowercased now keeps its case, e.g. `OMRS_EXTRA_Initializer_DOMAINS` used to set `initializer.domains` and now sets `Initializer.DOMAINS`. Such names need to be written all upper case, or in the property's exact case.
- Anyone who escaped backslashes in these variables by hand to work around the old handling will now get doubled backslashes.

**Not covered:** non-ASCII values. The install script is read with `Properties.load(InputStream)` (ISO-8859-1) and runtime properties as UTF-8.

## Testing

No automated tests cover `startup-init.sh`. I ran the properties section of the script under `bash -aeu` for both a first install and an existing runtime properties file, and loaded the output with `java.util.Properties` as OpenMRS does:

- On `master`, each of the four problems reproduces.
- On this branch, a value containing `\t`, `\\`, `=`, `:`, `#`, leading spaces, CR and LF, and a DB password containing `\`, read back exactly as set on both paths. Mixed-case and duplicate names behave as described above.
